title: Wigan Council: QuickAction in adult social care
summary: Wigan Council reports that Agilisys QuickAction tools saved an estimated 107 staff days on minutes and made 4,500 tenant survey responses usable for analysis.
account: Wigan and Agilisys developed QuickAction workflows for care assessments, minutes, audits and analysis of free-text surveys. On 2 January 2025 the council reported that automation halved the time spent on minute-taking and saved an estimated 107 days of staff work. It also reported analysis of 4,500 tenant responses that could not previously be processed in aggregate. The council's account presents reduced sickness, recruitment and overtime as projections. It provides no independent outcome evaluation. In its assessment published on 18 March 2026, the Care Quality Commission found that Wigan had introduced AI tools for note-taking, case audits and resident advice. Staff told the regulator that the note-taking tools helped them focus on people during assessments and reduced administrative burden. The regulator found that case records produced with the AI assessment tool captured detailed and personalized conversations. It gives no time or cost figures. In the same assessment the regulator rated Wigan's adult social care outstanding. Agilisys later reported £72,000 in savings from automated minutes and stated that more than 300 social workers use the tools daily. These figures come from the maker.
purpose: Reduce social-care administration and make qualitative feedback usable for service teams.
